transcript:
User: Yeah, what.
Agent: Hey, I’m Linda on Jay’s team at Dialux — what made you call in today?
User: Didn't call. You called me. Why?
Agent: Got it, thanks for picking up then.  

Yeah, I’d called because we work with businesses that are losing customers when calls go unanswered, and I wanted to see if that’s been an issue for you at all — do you ever miss calls when you or your team are tied up?
User: Sure, sure. Miss a few calls.
Agent: Yeah, makes sense, most businesses do. When those calls go to voicemail, do people usually leave a message or do they just hang up and move on?
User: Most hang up. Rarely leave messages.
Agent: Got it, so most of those callers just disappear.  

When the phone rings and you’re tied up, who’s supposed to be answering it right now — is it mainly you, or do you have someone at the front/office handling calls?
User: Me. No front office. Just me and sons.
Agent: Gotcha, so it’s all on you and your boys right now.  

When you miss those calls, what do you feel it costs you more — lost jobs/revenue, or just extra headaches trying to call people back later?
User: Lost jobs, mostly. Headaches too. Fewer bookings.
Agent: Yeah, that tracks — lost jobs, headaches, fewer bookings... it all stacks up.  

So when a new job calls in and you’re out working, what usually happens — does the call just ring out and they move on to the next company?
User: Unbelievable. Yeah, they probably call elsewhere. Typical.
Agent: Yeah… that’s the killer, right? Every missed call is basically handing a job to the next guy.  

Rough guess for you — on a normal week, how many calls do you think you and your sons miss that end up going nowhere?
User: About 9 missed calls a week.
Agent: Yeah, missing around 9 a week adds up fast — that’s a lot of jobs just slipping away.  

If even a couple of those each week turned into booked work automatically without you picking up, would that actually move the needle for you, or would it be more “nice to have”?
User: Sure, sure. Would probably help. Maybe half would've booked.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — even half of those would change things.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what that adds up to in dollars, or no one’s shown you the math yet?
User: No one's shown me. Don't care for math chit-chat.
Agent: Totally fair, we don’t have to geek out on numbers.  

So instead of math — if you could stop those 9 missed calls a week from leaking to competitors and turn them into booked jobs automatically, is that something you’d actually want to fix, or are you more “it is what it is” about it?
User: Fine, fine. Bookings are better. Fix it, I guess.
Agent: Gotcha, so you’re leaning toward “let’s actually fix this” rather than just living with it.  

So… it’s a quick 20‑minute walkthrough where we show you how to stop losing those 9 calls a week and turn them into booked jobs — what’s better for you this week: later today or tomorrow?
User: Unbelievable. Tomorrow, I guess. Afternoon's better.
Agent: Got it, tomorrow afternoon works.  

Before I lock in a time with Jay, what’s your first name?
User: Gene. Szymanski. Owner of Szymanski & Sons Plumbing.
Agent: Alright Gene, I can get you in tomorrow in the afternoon — we’ve got a spot at 1:00 or 1:45 Central; which works better for you?
User: Sure, sure. 1:45 Central.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: One more moment while I lock that in.
Agent: Alright Gene, looks like the calendar’s giving us trouble on that 1:45 spot, so here’s what we’ll do — Jay or someone from our team will call you directly at this number within the hour to lock in that same time for tomorrow. Thanks for rolling with the tech hiccup today, and we’ll talk to you soon.
